subject: Minimum number of frequency for estimating item fit statistics (dichotomous data)

messages.author: f61de5f78c7e0a18
messages.subject: Minimum number of frequency for estimating item fit statistics (dichotomous data)
parts:
Dear Phi,

I am fitting a unidimentional 2PL model for 25 dichotomous items scored as 0 for failure and 1 for success.  When I ask for item fit statistics NA is produced for four items.  These items have extremely low frequency of failure (0) in relative to success (1). For example one item has 4 cases with 0 and 499 with 1.  So I would like to ask a) if this large discripance is responsible for not producing item fit statistics and b) what might be the minimum expected counts for calcuations of the item fit statistics.

Thanks a lot,

Nikos

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Minimum number of frequency for estimating item fit statistics (dichotomous data)
parts:
Hi Nikos,

It's too difficult to answer this question specifically since it depends on a number of data/model characteristics, though the way you described the setup certainly does sound problematic in the the number of valid observed/expected category counts will probably be much less than the degrees of freedom for the chi-squared statistics. You could try playing around the the expected count threshold defaults in itemfit(), though in general the more aggressive the expected value tolerance the less chi-square the detection statistics will behave.

Phil
